title: Method for generating high-quality tetrahedral meshes of geological models by utilizing CGAL
author: Wang, Mei, et al.

steps.title: Validate triangulated surface input
steps.instruction: Check that the geological model consists only of triangulated surfaces that are non‑self‑intersecting, that any two surfaces are either disjoint or share only border edges, and that no isolated points are present; if two surfaces intersect, the intersection must be represented as a 1‑dimensional feature.

steps.title: Determine surface orientation
steps.instruction: For each triangulated surface, identify its positive (exterior) and negative sides by selecting any point located inside the corresponding subdomain and using CGAL::orientation(p, q, r, s) where p, q, r are the vertices of a facet and s is the interior point; the sign returned defines the orientation of the whole surface.

steps.title: Construct subdomain index pairs
steps.instruction: Assign an integer index to every subdomain (exterior index 0, interior subdomains 1…N). For each surface, record the subdomain index on its positively oriented side and the index on its negatively oriented side, creating an ordered pair (positive_index, negative_index) that follows the order in which the surfaces are stored.

steps.title: Generate tetrahedral mesh
steps.instruction: Configure CGAL mesh generation with user‑defined cell‑size (controls tetrahedron size) and facet‑size (controls surface facet size) criteria, run the Delaunay refinement, then apply the optimization phase consisting of ODT smoothing, Lloyd smoothing, sliver perturber, and sliver exuder in that order; ensure the initial surface mesh is conformal (no isolated points) so the method guarantees overall conformity; respect the relationship between required volume size and surface‑mesh size: if volume size < 0.5 × surface size, the surface mesh is refined; if 0.5 × surface size ≤ volume size ≤ surface size, the surface mesh is kept fixed; if volume size > surface size, ill‑shaped elements may appear and the volume size should be reduced to ≤ surface size; finally output the mesh file containing points, triangles, and tetrahedra.

substeps.instruction: Set cell‑size and facet‑size criteria according to user needs.
Run CGAL Delaunay refinement to create an initial volume mesh.
Check surface‑mesh conformity (no isolated points) – the algorithm enforces conformity automatically if the input surface is conformal.
Adjust surface refinement based on the ratio of required volume size to surface‑mesh size as described.
Write the resulting mesh (points, surface triangles, tetrahedra) to the chosen output format.

description: In this section, we will describe the implementation details of presented method for generating high-quality tetrahedral meshes of geological models.
